# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**To:** Cigna — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Riley Lawson
Member ID: W461122627
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-18 — Reference number POC-5D67837DC3-99680**
**Requested service:** ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888
**Denial reason given:** documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity
**Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-312 Knee Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026 (https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-312%20Knee%20Surg%20Arthro%20%26%20Open%20Proc_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf)

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing Cigna's denial of ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888), issued on 2026-08-18 under reference number POC-5D67837DC3-99680. I am asking Cigna to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed.

The notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete. I believe the records already in my file address each of the criteria in the plan's own policy, and I have set them side by side below so a reviewer can check them point by point. If any specific document is still missing, I ask that Cigna tell me exactly which one, so my surgeon's office can send it.

---

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. Imaging showing the ACL injury.** The policy criterion reads:

> "MRI, CT arthrogram, or arthroscopy shows a tear/disruption or significant laxity of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL)"

My MRI of the knee on 2026-06-28 showed a complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with a bone bruise pattern. The menisci were intact and there was no significant arthritis. A complete mid-substance tear on MRI is exactly the finding this criterion describes.

**2. Physical examination findings.** The policy criterion reads:

> "Physical exam demonstrates ANY of the following positive orthopedic tests/signs:"

My examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain. I note that this criterion ends in a colon and introduces a list of specific tests and signs that was not reproduced in the material available to me. I am therefore not able to match my exam to a named test from the policy text itself. I ask Cigna to identify which listed tests or signs it applied, and to confirm whether the documented positive provocative testing satisfies them — or to tell my surgeon which specific test result it needs.

**3. Function-limiting pain and loss of function.** The policy criterion reads:

> "function-limiting knee pain and/or loss of knee function which interferes with ANY of the following:"

This criterion also introduces a list. Two of the items on that list are quoted in the policy language available to me:

> "ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living"

> "need to return to activities that require cutting, pivoting, and/or agility in which ACL insufficiency may predispose to further instability episodes that may result in new articular or meniscal cartilage injuries"

My records document 18 months of progressive knee pain that is not relieved by rest, and recurrent instability with pivoting. My knee has given way twice on stairs. Stairs are part of ordinary daily life, and pivoting is the exact motion the second item describes.

**4. Reports of instability.** The policy criterion reads:

> "reports of knee instability which is noted as giving way, subjective weakness, or buckling."

My chart documents recurrent instability with pivoting and two episodes of the knee giving way on stairs. "Giving way" is the plan's own wording.

**5. Failure of non-surgical management.** The policy criterion reads:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration"

My conservative treatment is documented in the record:

- **Supervised physical therapy** for range of motion and quadriceps strengthening, with bracing — 16 weeks, from 2026-03-13 to 2026-07-03, 16 visits completed, recorded in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **NSAIDs** for 8 months, with inadequate relief.
- **Corticosteroid injection** on 2026-05-28, which gave 4 weeks of partial relief.

Sixteen weeks of provider-directed physical therapy is longer than the three months the policy asks for, and it was completed and documented before the authorization request. The NSAID trial and the injection are additional provider-directed non-surgical care. Despite all of it, my pain has continued to progress and my knee continues to give way.

**6. The criteria exception.** The policy also states:

> "Criteria exception: Three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is not required if there is an acute injury setting and joint instability has been documented with ANY of the following additional conditions:"

> "a confirmed ACL tear and a repairable meniscus tear"

> "concomitant ligament injuries (i.e., multi-ligamentous knee injury) that require reconstruction to provide stability"

I am not relying on this exception, and I am not claiming it applies to me — my MRI reports the menisci as intact. I quote it only to be complete, and to make the point that I do not need the exception, because the three months of provider-directed non-surgical management was in fact completed and documented.

---

## On the finding that the documentation was incomplete

I understand Cigna's notice to say that what was submitted did not allow a determination of medical necessity. The records summarized above were part of the prior authorization packet: a dated MRI report with a specific ACL finding, a dated physical therapy course with a visit count and a discharge note, dated medication and injection trials, documented instability episodes, and a documented examination. My surgeon has documented that the procedure is needed.

If Cigna's reviewer needs something further, I ask for two specific things:

1. A list of the exact documents or findings Cigna considers missing, so my surgeon's office can supply them promptly; and
2. Identification of which subsections of Cigna CMM-312 Knee Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026 were applied to my request — in particular the lists of orthopedic tests and signs, and the list of interfered-with activities, which follow the colons in the criteria quoted above and were not available to me.

I want to be straightforward about the limits of this letter: the quoted passages above are the only policy language I have. I have not quoted, and have not tried to reconstruct, any other part of the policy, and I have not assigned the plan any threshold, duration, or requirement that does not appear in the text I quoted.

---

## Closing request

I respectfully ask Cigna to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-18 (reference POC-5D67837DC3-99680) and authorize ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888, as requested by Dr. Lindqvist. If the denial is upheld in whole or in part, I ask for a written explanation identifying each criterion of Cigna CMM-312 Knee Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026 that Cigna finds unmet, the specific documentation Cigna requires to meet it, and information about my further appeal rights, including any right to external review.

Per my denial notice, my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice — by **2027-02-14**. I am submitting this appeal through my plan's appeal process: I can log in at my.cigna.com to find and submit my plan's appeal form, or call 1-800-244-6224 or the number on my card. Because the mailing address is plan-specific, I am using the appeal address printed on my denial letter.

I authorize Cigna to discuss this appeal with Dr. Lindqvist and that office's staff. Please send all correspondence to me at the address above.

Thank you for taking another look at my case.

Sincerely,

**Riley Lawson**
Member ID: W461122627
Date of birth: [My date of birth]
Reference number: POC-5D67837DC3-99680
Date: [Date signed]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-18
- MRI report, knee, 2026-06-28
- Physical therapy records and discharge note, 2026-03-13 to 2026-07-03
- Office notes from Dr. Lindqvist, including examination findings
- Medication and injection records, including corticosteroid injection 2026-05-28
- [Any additional records my surgeon's office is sending]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
